10.text: Micron's CEO expects memory supply to stay tight through 2028, with long-term deals extending past 2030 and strong pricing power amid AI-driven demand. Micron stock is down roughly 24-25% from its peak ahead of December earnings, and analysts debate whether its boom can continue.

9.text: Nvidia's valuation metrics have compressed sharply even as analysts project strong AI-driven revenue and earnings growth, with forward P/E near 14x and trailing P/E at 27x. The company authorized a $235 billion buyback, and shares closed at $217.09, up 1.38%, with Q3 EPS expected at $2.49.

6.text: AMD shares rose on TD Cowen’s buy rating and $675 target, after a 140%-plus 2026 run and a 13% drop last week on AI funding and data-center demand worries. One article says AMD has narrowed the gap with Nvidia via its MI450 GPUs.

17.text: Broadcom's custom AI chip revenue is surging with 50% margins, though its stock sits 35% below peak amid AI bubble warnings and TSMC capacity competition. Marvell raised fiscal 2028 guidance to $20 billion, targeting $70–90 billion by 2031, after a 170% yearly run and recent 17% dip.

19.text: Nvidia received over $35 billion in chip orders from ByteDance, Tencent, and Alibaba, and Elon Musk said SpaceX is adding 200,000 chips monthly. The stock swung between gains and a correction as investors weighed concentration risk and AI bubble concerns.

15.text: TSMC posted record Q3 results with revenue up 41% year over year and profit up 69%, saying AI demand exceeds its supply and upgrading forecasts. Chip stocks, including Nvidia peers, rebounded on October 19, while ASML reported demand stretching to 2030.

11.text: Nebius borrowed $3.5 billion, launched public spot GPU pricing, and expanded its Nvidia collaboration on secure AI agents. CoreWeave’s stock swung on debt concerns—$27.6 billion borrowed, projected 6.3x leverage—while SpaceX demand signals lifted neocloud shares.

12.text: Michael Burry disclosed bets against AI stocks including Nvidia, predicting a 2000-style rotation where market winners plunge. Articles also cite record S&P 500 CAPE ratios above 40 and warnings from Warren Buffett and crash historians about extreme overvaluation.
